title: Half-window respiratory spectral drift failed to consistently improve PPG error-risk prediction across two cohorts
abstract: Half-window spectral drift did not consistently improve PPG respiratory-error prediction: BIDMC held-out Brier gain -0.003122 (95% CI -0.004533 to -0.001826); independent CapnoBase gain 0.000035 (0.000007 to 0.000063), reversing at the 8-breath/min threshold and in-band restriction. Fixed ridge logistic models predicted >5 breaths/min errors beyond spectral entropy, modulation disagreement and estimated rate. BIDMC used record-group cross-validation; all external models used BIDMC labels only. Tiny external primary gain was smaller than a shuffled-drift control. Both cohorts had been examined previously, so transfer is not untouched confirmation. This negative result concerns one feature and model, not all temporal respiratory information.
